title: Evals change-inspector: temporal grouping + rate-limited notifications for regression alerts
creator: Marisol Vega
description: Build a Console-first ‘change inspector’ that ties eval regressions to concrete config and model changes and delivers high-signal notifications (Slack / PagerDuty) using temporal grouping and rate-limits. Goals: 1) correlate a measurable quality delta with the smallest set of config/model diffs across recent rollouts; 2) reduce noisy/frequent alerts by deduping within configurable time windows and by fingerprinting failing eval sets; 3) provide one-click remediation links (pin model, rollback rollout, mute alert) and an audit trail for compliance teams. Primary consumers: SREs, ML platform owners, and product owners who operate model-serving in Dedicated/Private and Hosted tiers.
acceptance_criteria: Console shows a ‘Change Inspector’ panel on the Evals dashboard that lists candidate changes (model version, quantization profile, batching settings, routing policy) correlated with the regression

Notifications to Slack channels and PagerDuty are suppressed when an identical fingerprinted regression has already fired within a configurable window (default 30m), with an option to escalate on repeat occurrences
Alerts include: delta metric (absolute + percent), example failing traces, link to the eval run, link to the rollout and model pin/rollback action, and RCA checklist
Admins can configure per-project noise_floor (min delta to alert), fingerprinting sensitivity, and dedupe window without engineering deploys
End-to-end tests validate dedupe across rapid sequential config flips and across parallel rollout instances (canary/A-B)
Telemetry emitted: alert_fired, alert_suppressed(reason), alert_escalated, inspector_match_score; available in console telemetry stream
notes: Design opened a scoping doc (Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/Evals-Change-Inspector) with early mocks. Engineering feasibility spike (ENG-2891) indicated need for a lightweight fingerprinting service and a compact change-diff API from rollout service. UX working group session scheduled 2026-02-20.
implementation_notes: Fingerprint: compute sorted hash over failing prompt IDs + normalized failure signature (metric, threshold breached) to identify duplicate alerts across runs
Temporal grouping: sliding window dedupe with per-team override; treat independent rollouts as separate unless share the same model-version + config-hash
Notification pipeline: fanout to Slack with thread-based aggregation, to PagerDuty with dedupe key = fingerprint + project; include action buttons for pin/rollback linked to console RBAC endpoints
Rollout link must include query params to pre-populate rollback target and show confidence metrics (throughput, latency, token cost)
Provide a ‘noise floor’ UI in project settings and expose an API for platform automation to adjust thresholds based on runtime SLOs
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (spike + infra): lightweight fingerprinting service + change-diff API (2 wks). Phase 2 (backend + telemetry): compute match scores, emit telemetry, expose dedupe config (3 wks). Phase 3 (Console + Notifications): dashboard panel + Slack/PagerDuty integration + action buttons (3 wks). Phase 4 (QA + rollouts): integration tests, staged rollout to internal accounts, collect feedback (2 wks).
risks: False negatives: over-aggressive dedupe may suppress distinct regressions — mitigated by match_score and escalation on repeats
Operational load: fingerprint service must be highly available and low-latency — plan to colocate with eval ingestion path
Security: notification action links must honor RBAC and short-lived tokens to prevent unauthorized rollbacks
